A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the platelet activation induced by shear stress is a function of shear stress and exposure, and the power law model is a useful tool to predict the PA in the range of well-defined shear stresses and exposure times.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the platelet activation induced by high mechanical shear stresses for short exposure time can be reliably detected by flow cytometry using surface P-selectin and PMPs as markers, and the power law model is a good approximation of the quantitative relationship between shear stress, exposure time and platelet activation.

the platelet activation in the high shear stress region can be quantitatively described by a power law model with a shear stress exponent of approximately 0.5, and the activation is highly dependent on the exposure time.
the shear-induced PA in human blood can be reliably quantified with surface P-selectins, and, to some extent, PMP.
